1 November 2026, Australia/Brisbane
Root-owned construction, ordinary proofs, complete instruments and costs.

RESULT AND STATUS
=================

The strongest construction in this continuation is a finite-duration,
finite-strength parity measurement whose entire intended output field carries
only Z1 Z2. It uses three finite harmonic modes, two ordinary reciprocal
beam-splitter couplings, one dispersive qubit-mode coupling, and two actual
longitudinal qubit-mode drives. All auxiliary modes return to vacuum at the
end of the same operation. No stationary spectral approximation, eliminated
receiver, infinitely fast feedback, or unobserved final apparatus is used.

For vacuum initial auxiliaries and vacuum reservoirs, the controlled coherent
state dilation is exact at every finite drive strength within this Hamiltonian
model. It proves preservation of arbitrary superpositions within BOTH parity
sectors, not only correct reported parity or equality of basis-state outlet
marginals. Finite detection efficiency affects assignment, but does not by
itself leak within-parity information through the main output.

Intrinsic auxiliary losses are retained exactly. Their unobserved part gives
an explicit error functional. Accessible losses can instead be corrected from
their photon records with only local Pauli/Z rotations. Their no-click rates
are independent of the logical state. The full binned measurement instrument
is composed into a CNOT with nonzero helper, local-gate and readout errors.

This is a mathematically complete operation in a stated effective model. It
is NOT a demonstrated lower-resource fault-tolerant computer or a validated
hardware proposal. Ordinary optimized control improves its first waveform.

1 November 2026. Root's construction, independently checked by finite_operation.

This replaces the ideal directional cascade in FINITE_OPERATION_REPORT.txt
with an explicit third oscillator. The two-mode derivation and its informative
predecessors remain preserved; the strongest selected construction is now the
finite reciprocal network below. No adiabatic elimination, zero-delay
circulator, ideal conditional scattering, or stationary tail is used.

Physical model
--------------
Let b,c be two auxiliary oscillators, m the engineered lossy readout oscillator,
and S=Z1 Z2. The Hamiltonian and outlets are

 H=g[(b^dag+c^dag)m+m^dag(b+c)]+chi Z1 c^dag c
       +u(t)Z2(b+b^dag)+w(t)Z2(c+c^dag),
 Lm=sqrt(Gamma)m, Lb=sqrt(kb)b, Lc=sqrt(kc)c.

All modes and input baths initially are vacuum. The physical resources are two
conditional longitudinal drives associated with Z2, one dispersive Z1-c link,
two finite beam-splitter couplings g, and one engineered lossy mode. Intrinsic
b/c loss is included as kb,kc. Nonlinear/saturation corrections, thermal input,
data-qubit noise, and implementation errors require their own budget.

Exact finite-time inverse construction
--------------------------------------
Define a real smooth U(t) with derivatives through the required order zero at
both endpoints. Root uses U proportional to sin^6(pi t/T). Set

 A=sqrt(Gamma)/g [U'+kb U/2],
 V=-(A'+Gamma A/2)/(g sqrt(Gamma))-U,
 B=[-kc V/2+g A/sqrt(Gamma)-V']/chi,
 u=-B'-kb B/2,
 w=B'+kc B/2-chi V.

The exact branch amplitudes are

 b_z=U s+iB z2,
 c_z=V s-iB z2,
 m_z=iA s/sqrt(Gamma).

Substituting directly into the THREE finite coupled oscillator equations proves
these identities. The engineered main output is exactly iA(t)S at every time.
All three modes return to vacuum, and the conditional drives vanish at both
endpoints. Initial/final limits follow from the sin^6 envelope; no final gauge
